pool.text: Dutch explorers sighted the Australian coast near present-day Perth, calling it Dedelsland.
Dutch Captain Willem de Vlamingh conducted the first documented exploration of the Perth region.
Captain James Stirling founded Perth as the administrative centre of the Swan River Colony.
The colony accepted transported convicts to supply labour for public works and construction.
Queen Victoria proclaimed Perth as a city after being named after Scotland.
Third Swamp was officially gazetted as a public park covering fifteen hectares.
Indigenous people were prohibited from entering large swathes of Perth under penalty of imprisonment.
Two-thirds of Western Australians voted in a referendum to secede from Australia.
Perth Festival started as Australia's longest running annual cultural festival held annually.
Perth received global media attention when residents lit house lights for astronaut John Glenn.
The Kewdale Freight Terminal was developed adjacent to the Welshpool industrial area.
Murdoch University was founded, incorporating Western Australia's only veterinary school.
Australia II won the America's Cup and is housed in Perth.
Perth became Australia's fourth-most populated city.
The University of Notre Dame Australia was established.
Novelist Tim Winton published Cloudstreet, making Perth the setting for the work.
The Perth Convention and Exhibition Centre was built as part of urban development.
The Kwinana Desalination Plant was opened to provide water resources.
The Federal Court ruled that Noongar native title persisted over the Perth metropolitan area.
The Diwali celebration in Perth attracted over 20,000 visitors.
